issues.detail: The Greek 'περικαλυψαντες' (perikalypsantes) means 'having covered/veiled around,' while the Vietnamese 'che mặt' (covered face) is too specific. The Greek refers to covering his head/face with a garment, but the Vietnamese phrasing makes it sound like they were specifically concealing his facial features.

The Greek 'ο παισας' (ho pais) is the nominative form of 'the boy/child.' The Vietnamese 'kẻ đã đánh ngươi' (the one who hit you) changes the subject from a specific person ('the boy') to an action ('the one who hit').
